newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia rural commodity prices improve-Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Australia rural commodity prices improve-Dresdner.

text.p: The National Farmers' Federation -Dresdner Australia Commodity Price Index released on Monday shows that Australian rural prices are at a 22 month high.

NFF director of economic policy Todd Ritchie said the Dresdner Commodity Price Index measured in Special Drawing Rights (SDR) terms, fell by 1.3 percent in April. However, in Australian dollar terms the index fell only 0.5 percent because of a slightly weaker Australian dollar during the month. The index was now 5.2 percent higher than a year ago, Ritchie said.

Rural SDR prices improved by 0.4 percent during April and are now 6.7 percent higher than a year ago, the result of strengthening sheep meat prices and modest gains for barley, sugar, wheat and wool, he said. These improvements were offset to some extent by weaker prices for rice, beef and cotton.
Ritchie said stronger than expected international demand, combined with extreme weather conditions in North America, had resulted in stronger wheat prices over the past month.

"Australian Standard White pool estimates for the 1996/97 crop rose by A$2.00 to A$200.00 per tonne last week, and most of the 1996/97 pool prices have risen by around A$2.00 a tonne," Ritchie said. Wool prices have also continued to improve with the Eastern Market Indicator moving above 620 cents a kg.
The wool market had taken on a more positive tone, with the stockpile slowly declining to 1.8 million bales and demand picking up, Ritchie said.
